title: Consumption commit protocol for retry-safe billing
creator: Lydia Chen
description:
Problem: transient client and network retries against inference endpoints lead to at-least-once ingestion semantics which can double-count tokens and cause incorrect billed consumption. Current mitigations (short-term retry dedupe in the ingest gateway) are partial and do not cover cross-region retries, delayed replays from load balancers, or server-side retries during replica failover.

Goal: implement a production-grade consumption commit protocol that guarantees logical once-only accounting for billing and quota consumption across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. The protocol should be resilient to client retries, request timeouts, server restarts, and transient partitioning while avoiding significant throughput regressions.

High-level approach: introduce a small, append-only consumption commit ledger per-customer (customer_id) with idempotency keys and commit states (tentative -> committed -> settled). Serving runtime writes a minimal "consumption intent" record synchronously before deducting tokens internally, then a short-lived commit step finalizes the ledger entry once the response is acknowledged. Reconciliation jobs validate ledger vs token balances and correct any divergences into a compensating ledger event (reverse or credit). Integrate with rate limiter by consulting the ledger's head when allocating capacity and by treating uncommitted intents as soft-reserved capacity to avoid overcommit.

Implementation notes: single new table (consumption_commits) with primary key (customer_id, commit_id) and columns as small strings: commit_id (client-provided idempotency key or server-generated nonce), status, tokens_consumed, route, created_at, finalize_at. Partition by customer hash for write scalability. Lightweight leader lease per-partition to coordinate finalization where needed. TTL for intents: 7 days for audit/rollback.

Why not pure global nonce service: we considered a central nonce coordinator but rejected it due to cross-region latency and single point of failure risk. The per-customer commit ledger is sharded and can be colocated with serving nodes to keep write latency < 5ms for hot customers.

Backward compatibility: For customers with legacy consumption paths, we will run a compatibility adapter that emits commit records asynchronously and flags them as settled after reconciliation; these customers will be rate-limited conservatively until fully migrated.
acceptance_criteria: New consumption_commits table exists and is partitioned by customer hash
Serving runtime writes intent and finalize paths for all hosted API generation and embedding flows
Billing pipeline reads only committed entries as primary source of truth for token deduction
Reconciler runs daily and surface any discrepancy alerts to billing dashboard
Unit/integration tests for retry scenarios (client retries, LB replay, server restart) demonstrating no double billing
Rollout strategy documented and smoke-tested on internal org before public rollout
design_notes: Intent-first flow: write small intent row with idempotency key before response streaming begins
Finalize path attempts to transition intent->committed. If finalize fails, reconciler will determine final settlement after timeout
Soft-reserve semantics: rate limiter treats intents as reserved but expires them after configurable window
Partitioning strategy: customer hash -> 1024 partitions, colocate partitions with serving shards where load is heavy
Optimizations: use compact binary encoding for commit_id and small integer types for tokens to reduce storage and replication bandwidth
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): deploy commit ledger read/write in canary region for internal org only (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (selected customers): enable for heavy customers behind Redwood Dedicated and measure latency/cost impact (4 weeks)
Phase 3 (gradual): flip default for hosted traffic over 8 waves, monitor billing diffs and SLOs
Fallback: gateway-level dedupe remains enabled; in case of regressions, we can disable finalization for new customers while preserving ledger entries for offline reconciliation
risks: Throughput regression for extreme QPS customers if finalization adds synchronous writes — mitigated by colocating partitions and batching finalizes
Increased storage and replication cost for commit ledger — mitigate with TTL and compact encoding
Complexity in migration for private deployments with air-gapped databases — provide adapter and migration playbook
Edge cases where late replays after TTL may still cause disputes — handled via reconciler and customer support manual adjustments
comments: 2025-10-29 - LC: Initial spike showed intent write adds ~3ms median latency in canary. Using colocated partitions reduced p95 impact to ~7ms.

2025-10-31 - MA: Reviewed partitioning and leader lease approach. Suggested moving finalize attempts to background for streaming responses where low latency matters; we'll attempt immediate finalize for short requests and background finalize for long streams.
2025-11-02 - PM (Sofia Patel): Need a clear UX for customers to see tentative vs committed charges in console. Added console-2025.11 to release labels.
2025-11-04 - Security (Anika Rao): KMS integration required for commit_id stable hashing if customer chooses opaque ids. Marking security_review_required: true in follow-up ticket.
2025-11-05 - LC: Implemented reconciler prototype; nightly job flags 0.02% of intents as unsettled in canary org — investigating root causes (mostly LB double-posts).
